propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing loops in claim.py and transition.py must be mechanically refactored to use stdlib argparse while preserving exact observable behavior

The --force flag requires command-specific semantics preservation: claim's bare --force consumes next non-option token; transition's bare --force sets force_reason='' and does not consume following tokens

The --assignee flag must preserve None-vs-empty-string sentinel: absent yields None (triggering default_assignee fallback), explicit empty string '' clears the assignee, and value-less exits with code 1
transition._parse_flags must be retained as an argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple to preserve three external direct callers in test files

argparse configuration must enforce: add_help=False (--help remains dispatcher-served byte-exact), allow_abbrev=False (exact-token matching only), parse_known_args (unknown tokens silently skipped), and custom error() override that raises CommandError(returncode=1) instead of argparse's exit-2
Retired --force-close flag must keep its exit-1 rejection with bespoke error message; module-size and complexity ratchets must stay within established thresholds
